title: Barclays5
summary: On 21 August 2026, the judge ruled out terrorist-connection sentencing in the Barclays5 case: the damage was not serious enough in the terrorism sense. Sentence for criminal damage had not been reported by 25 October. The earlier reporting is retained below as a historical record.
review_note: The August 2026 ruling supersedes the July dossier’s suggestion that terrorist-connection sentencing remained a possibility in this case. Read the update above first. The wider imported dossier, subsequent sentence and any appeal status have not had a full current-status review.

updates.title: Judge rules out terrorist-connection sentencing
updates.summary: On 21 August 2026, HHJ Altham at Preston Crown Court ruled that section 69 of the Sentencing Act 2020 did not apply to the Barclays5 case.
paragraphs: The judge found that the damage, although significant, did not meet the high threshold of serious damage in the statutory definition of terrorism (ruling, paragraphs 45–50 and 56). The damage cost £177,337, a little over £200,000 including VAT (paragraph 1).

The question arose only after the verdicts. On 22 June 2026 the trial judge asked both sides for submissions on section 69, and the Crown argued for a terrorist connection on 8 July (paragraphs 3 and 19). The judge rejected the defence arguments that raising it after conviction was unfair (paragraphs 36–43); the case turned on the seriousness of the damage.

This was a decision about sentencing, not an acquittal of criminal damage. The judge expressly limited the decision to these facts; it does not rule out terrorist-connection findings in other cases (paragraph 51).

Sentence for criminal damage: the ruling records that sentence was adjourned to 4 September 2026 (paragraph 2). Declassified UK reported on 21 August that sentencing was scheduled for 30 October. As of 25 October 2026 we have not found a report of the sentence.

The July headlines and commentary below describe a sentencing proposal that the court subsequently rejected. This update confirms the August ruling only; later sentencing and appeal outcomes have not been verified here. For how section 69 works and how this ruling compares with Filton, read our legal study, Terrorist connection add-on.

sources.title: ‘Barclays 5’ Palestine activists will not be tried as terrorists

body_html:
Five defendants — Brendon O’Hagan and Mohammed Malik, both 28; Amanda Kelly and Hmeera Atiqnisar, both 31; and Alma Yaniv, 70 — convicted of criminal damage at Preston Crown Court over an August 2024 action at a Barclays branch in Burnley. The CPS applied for a “terrorist connection” finding only after the trial had concluded.

  • Activists Who Spray-Painted Barclays Set to Be Sentenced as Terrorists Novara Media · 27 July 2026 Left novaramedia.com/2026/07/27/activists-who-spray-painted-barclays-set-to-be-sentenced-as-terrorists/
  • Five protesters convicted of criminal damage face sentencing as terrorists Middle East Eye · 27 July 2026 middleeasteye.net/news/five-protesters-convicted-criminal-damage-face-sentencing-terrorists
  • Five more Palestine activists could be sentenced as terrorists Declassified UK · 27 July 2026 declassifieduk.org/five-more-palestine-activists-could-be-sentenced-as-terrorists/ Has the court-filing detail that the CPS applied only after the trial ended. Interview with Atiqnisar.
  • Judge moves to sentence Barclays spray painters as terrorists despite no terror charges Free the Filton 25 · campaign site Campaign filtonactionists.com/judge-moves-to-sentence-barclays-spray-painters-as-terrorists-despite-no-terror-charges/ Fullest account of the sequence, including the judge circulating Justice Johnson’s Filton ruling to defence counsel. Partisan — corroborate before relying on it.
  • PA wire copy, syndicated Press Association via Yahoo Agency ca.news.yahoo.com/palestine-action-activists-ransacked-barclays-073012794.html The neutral agency version most outlets ran. Best single citation for the bare facts.
  • Palestine Action Barclays bank — sentenced as terrorists The Jewish Chronicle Hostile thejc.com/news/uk/palestine-action-barclays-bank-sentenced-terrorists-rga3642x Unsympathetic to the defendants and confirms the same underlying facts. Valuable for exactly that reason.
